_readme: Events and Multimedia Production, Version 1.2: the page's words and its media configuration, section by section (src/pages/work/events-video.astro and src/components/events/). Copy follows John's Combined Build Brief and the V1.1 and V1.2 delta briefs (October 14, 2026) and the facts in his working log; no metric is published until it has been verified, and nothing here mentions an unannounced pilot, contract or Foundation discussions, investor diligence, data rooms or fundraising. Media slots name asset ids in src/data/assets.json: to replace a placeholder, drop the file in and approve its entry there; the layout never changes, because every slot already holds its final aspect ratio. Unapproved slots show a labeled placeholder in `npm run dev` only and nothing in a production build.

hero._hero: One editorial reel (V1.2), in place of V1.1's three programs and their control: the chapters below, in this order, each one video cut from the brief's ranges (assets.json has each chapter's ranges and edits), played through once and crossfaded (350ms) into the next, round and round, muted. The label at the top left of the frame reads the chapter's number and title, numbered in order among the chapters whose video is approved and present: the team interview's chapter is pending, so it is left out entirely (no placeholder) and the chapters after it carry the lower numbers until its video is added. `pos` places the crop of the wide cinematic frame on each video (object-position), chosen so the burned-in captions stay whole and clear of the rail, and heads stay in, at both of the frame's proportions (2.2:1, and 2.4:1 on shorter wide screens); `fitNarrow` is how the video fills the 16:9 frame on narrow screens.
hero.headline: From live experience to lasting momentum.
hero.copy: I turn live opportunities into complete marketing systems, from sponsorship and on-site production to content, distribution, and the relationships that continue after the room clears.

transition._transition: Replaces the run of show (V1.1): the five stages as one phrase, revealed word by word over about seven tenths of a screen of scrolling, held, then straight into the activation. On small screens it breaks into two lines after `break` words.

activation.headline: The work starts before anyone enters the room.
activation.copy: Bolt Liquidity sponsored the Sui Summit side event at ETHDenver in 2025 and 2026. Before the doors opened, I negotiated the sponsorship and its pricing, coordinated with the event host, sourced and priced the merchandise, worked with design on the screen animations and table assets, and planned how all of it would reach the people in the room.
activation._visual: An original 3D render of the activation (V1.1, replacing the schematic): a representative visualization, not a photograph, made for this page in Blender (scripts/render/; the spatial and lighting reference is reference/events-video/booth-render.png, never published). The television and the projected wall play their loops while the frame is in view; reduced motion, a data-saving preference, a small screen or no JavaScript keep the render with both screens on their poster frames.
activation.caption: A representative rendering of the activation, made for this page.

room.headline: Build the session. Fill the room. Extend its life.
room.copy: I organized and ran Bolt Liquidity’s presentation at Sui Summit in both 2025 and 2026. The recording here is from 2026, captured from the room as the session ran.

Captured the presentation from multiple angles

Used the session to support continued ecosystem conversations

room.outcome: The presentation attracted ecosystem attention and opened conversations that continued beyond the event.

setup.headline: A compact setup. A full content system.
setup.copy: At ETHDenver I booked a production room at the venue and built a studio from what was on hand: a DJI camera and an iPhone on two tripods, a clip-on microphone, a laptop, the venue’s lighting and props. I wrote about 20 interview questions and directed Max McKendry through multiple takes. The finished explainers came from what happened after the session: the footage review, the takes I chose, and the edit direction I wrote for Bob van der Meer.

credits._credits: One consolidated block per major chapter (V1.1), never one per media item: the Sui Summit work at ETHDenver (the activation, the session and the production room) closes the production room; Sui Fest keeps its own. V1.2 folded the section on what continued after into the conclusion, and its credit block with it.

items.what: Sponsorship negotiation and pricing, logistics, merchandise sourcing, production planning, the speaking slot, session strategy, deck direction, live production, the production room and equipment, interview questions, direction, camera capture, footage review, transcript-based edit briefs, and distribution
Screen animations and table assets, made in collaboration
Deck design, final video editing, and visual production

suifest.headline: If you cannot own the stage, create the moment everyone shares.
suifest.copy: Bolt was not a sponsor at Sui Fest, so the opportunity had to be made. I developed an interview concept, stepped in front of the camera as the interviewer, and spoke with established teams across the ecosystem, with Bolt as one voice among many. Every team in the piece was tagged, which gave each a reason to share it, and placed Bolt as a contributor to the ecosystem rather than a spectator at its edge.
suifest._video: Muted by default (V1.1): it plays silently while in view, with motion allowed, and the reader turns the sound on.

outcome._outcome: Distribution and performance in one block (V1.1), from the brief's qualitative facts only; a verified figure joins it once its metric entry is approved.
outcome.label: What it did
outcome.lead: Tens of thousands of impressions. Hundreds of likes.
outcome.line: Published with every team tagged and then shared by the teams themselves, it drew engagement from ecosystem teams and developers.

conclusion._conclusion: V1.2: the conclusion and the former Amplify section (Every event opens a longer conversation.) in one closing: the static row of the five stages as a quiet callback (never animated a second time), the headline, one paragraph, then the way on to the next case study in order, Creator Campaigns (the collection wraps around), then Contact.
conclusion.headline: The room clears. The work keeps moving.
conclusion.copy: An event is only the starting point. I turn live moments into content, extend their reach through partner and ecosystem distribution, and carry that momentum into strategic relationships and new opportunities.
conclusion.nextLine: Next, see how I build creator partnerships into campaigns designed to travel.
